builds.message:
studio: isolate workflow tests, conservative gone-detection, synced version

- the export/import test wrote into the real plugin workflows folder
  (GraphStore follows STUDIO_PLUGINS_ROOT): a fixed name could overwrite
  a user's selftest-t2v.json and a mid-test failure leaked files. It
  now runs against a tmp copy of the plugin (isolation via
  STUDIO_PLUGINS_ROOT), uses uuid-suffixed names and sweeps leftovers
  in finally.
- _remote_gone() no longer treats a textual 'not found' as a deleted
  upstream: GitHub answers exactly that for live private repositories
  the caller lost access to. Only a definitive local-path answer is
  'gone'; everything else stays 'unavailable'.
- WanGPStudioPlugin.version now reads plugin_info.json instead of a
  stale class constant (was 1.3.0).

ci: install the MMGP runtime dependencies the vendored suite needs

The WanFlow UI suite pulls shared.attention -> mmgp.offload, which
imports accelerate and optimum.quanto; the CI env stopped the suite at
collection with 'No module named accelerate'. requirements.txt pins
these as MMGP deps: accelerate>=1.1.1, optimum-quanto==0.2.7,
transformers==4.54.0, safetensors, filelock, comfy-kitchen==0.2.35
(full requirements.txt is intentionally not installed - CUDA-only
packages). Both jobs get the same set.

studio: remote-gone vs unavailable, host compatibility verdict (1.3.3)

- a failed fetch no longer claims the upstream is deleted: Plugin
  Health probes the remote once (ls-remote) and only the server's own
  'not found' answer yields upstream-gone / fork-detached; DNS,
  timeout or auth trouble yields fork-unavailable / stale-refs
- new host_wan2gp_version() reads the WanGP_version constant from
  wgp.py (no import), and every entry now carries wangp_compatible -
  the UI flags plugins whose declared wan2gp_version exceeds the host
- verified on this installation: H3 Director is current after its
  origin was repointed at the maintained public copy
  (HateTM/MiniMax-H3-Director, local == b27729d); suites: 203 passed

plugin-manager: follow tracking branches and refuse dirty updates

- update_plugin() resolved the remote ref by the local branch name, so
  a checkout on fix/civitai-filters tracking origin/main could not
  resolve its remote branch at all. The update now follows
  branch.tracking_branch() and only falls back to the local name.
- updates are refused while the checkout carries uncommitted changes:
  a pull over dirty work is a guaranteed mess, untracked files are
  still allowed.
- regression tests for both, incl. the finetune-manager scenario
  (named branch tracking origin/main) and the clean-pull path.

studio: self-sufficient export/import test and required WanFlow in CI

test_export_import_routes_against_installed_plugin assumed a
user-created workflow (draft-video-t2v) that the fork's .gitignore
excludes as runtime data: green locally, 404 on the vendored CI
checkout. The test now builds its workflow through the real import
route, exports it, re-imports under another name and deletes both.

The main Studio tests job also sets WANFLOW_UI_REQUIRED=1: with the
plugin vendored, a broken WanFlow import must fail the run instead of
silently skipping tests.

ci: vendor the wanflow-ui fork so integration tests run by default

plugins/wan2gp-wanflow-ui (reconciled fork 0.2.0 @ d9087bf, see its
RECONCILIATION.md) is now tracked in this repository via a .gitignore
negation, following the existing wan2gp-ming-image precedent. Only the
fork's git-tracked files are staged: its own .gitignore keeps the
runtime workflows, blocks and output cache out of this repo, and the
nested .git history stays local for future reconciliations.

- studio tests: the workflow tests no longer skip on CI - the vendored
  plugin ships with the checkout; WANFLOW_UI_REQUIRED=1 stays for the
  opt-in integration job that checks out an alternate WanFlow version
  (WANFLOW_UI_REPO variable), so the variable is no longer needed for
  the default pipeline
- new CI step runs the vendored fork's own suite (98 tests) against
  current WanGP on every push
- vendoring mechanics note: git silently no-ops 'git add' for files
  under a directory whose nested .git exists; the .git must be moved
  aside for the add and restored after

studio: fork-detached state for locally maintained plugins

A dead remote with local commits on top (MiniMax-H3-Director: upstream
repo deleted, 3 local fixes) is a maintained fork, not a broken plugin:
Plugin Health now reports fork-detached instead of stale-refs after a
failed fetch.

studio: Plugin Health view with upstream comparison (1.3.2)

New Plugins view in Studio: every folder under plugins/ is classified
against its origin remote - installed vs upstream version, behind/ahead
counts, local commit titles, remote reachability - so plugin audits no
longer rely on plugin_info versions alone.

- plugin_health.py: offline snapshot from local git metadata plus a
  background fetch scan (cooldown-limited); states built-in / current
  / behind / fork / fork-diverged / stale-refs / unreachable / no-remote
- API: GET /api/plugins/health[?wait=1], POST /api/plugins/health/refresh
- UI: nav entry with a needs-attention badge, health table, refresh
  button polling the background scan
- verified against this installation: 15 current, 3 forks flagged
  (wanflow-ui, finetune-manager, H3-Director), 13 built-in

plugin-manager: version-first release compare and fork-guarded updates

- compare_release_metadata() now compares versions before dates: a newer
  version must win even when its date string is older or missing;
  dates decide only for equal versions (fixes shipped without a bump)
  or when a side has no usable version. The old date-first order let a
  stale catalog entry (Status Pro 1.0.2/2026-08-15) suppress update
  notices for a year of releases.
- update_plugin() refuses to pull when the checkout carries local-only
  commits (fork) or shares no history with origin (fork snapshot):
  a conflict-free auto-merge would fold local work into a merge
  commit silently. Affected installs today: wan2gp-wanflow-ui (5
  local commits), Wan2GP-finetune-manager (5), MiniMax-H3-Director (3).
- new plugins/plugin_manager/tests suite covers both; wired into the
  Studio tests workflow alongside the studio suite.

plugin-manager: refresh stale catalog versions against upstream

Plugin Manager compares (date, version) with the catalog first, so stale
entries suppress the update notice. Verified against each upstream repo
HEAD on 2026-11-04 and refreshed:

- Status Pro 1.0.2 -> 1.3.1 (upstream 73db27b, 2026-11-03)
- MiniMax H3 Prompt Builder 2.0.0 -> 4.1.0
- MiniMax H3 RefMods 0.22.0 -> 0.42.0
- Finetune Manager 3.6.3 -> 4.0.1 (installed copy is a local fork with
  5 own CivitAI commits: the notice is truthful, but reconcile before
  pulling)
- Prompt Library 0.2.0 -> 0.3.0

Local sweep also fast-forwarded clean checkouts: status-pro 1.2.1 ->
1.3.1, prompt library 0.3.0, RefMods 0.42.0, prompt builder 4.1.0.
Image Suite was already at upstream HEAD (723af72). MiniMax-H3-Director
upstream repo is gone (404). WanFlow UI is a fork with unrelated
histories (4 local commits) and stays untouched.

studio: SendTo reliability and media index hardening (1.3.1)

- sendToTarget opens the hand-off tab inside the user gesture and closes
  it when the API or bridge fails: with 'noopener' window.open always
  returns null, so popup blocking was indistinguishable from success
- SendTo targets are filtered by the manifest 'accepts' kinds and the
  plugin enabled state in the UI; create() and the bridge refuse
  disabled plugins instead of parking undeliverable hand-offs
- MediaIndex scans keep only entries whose insertion generation
  postdates the scan start: a deleted file with a future mtime no
  longer survives as a gallery ghost, and clock-skewed additions
  during a scan cannot be lost
- media list cards no longer expose absolute paths/root; the detail
  view and upload answer keep them for Copy path and the lightbox
- new 10k-file MediaIndex benchmark (STUDIO_MEDIA_BENCH=1): warm-up
  0.40s, first screen 173ms against the 2s roadmap budget
- version strings consistent across topbar, footer and plugin_info
studio: real SendTo hand-off and incremental media index (1.3.0)
studio: guard Run/Save handshake and scan-vs-index_file race (review follow-up)
ci: trigger workflows to verify manager-catalog repair and studio 1.2.2

studio: stabilize 1.2.2 (graph sync, comfyui links, ci deps, media hardening)

- toolbar Save/Run request the live graph from the canvas via get_graph
  handshake (4s timeout aborts instead of writing a stale graph)
- comfyui-ui export rebuilds links/inputs/outputs from graph.edges;
  canvas metadata is stored once per workflow (graph.ui.comfyui_ui) with
  a per-node fallback for older saves; no more dangling link ids
- validate postMessage origin ("null" for the sandboxed srcdoc frame);
  canvas answers only messages from window.parent
- CI: install diffusers==0.36.0 and pin all test deps (shared.utils
  imports diffusers at collection); optional studio-integration job
  driven by WANFLOW_UI_REPO/WANFLOW_UI_REF with WANFLOW_UI_REQUIRED=1
- media: _inside_roots resolves realpath (symlink escape rejected);
  uploads index a single file (MediaIndex.index_file) instead of a
  blocking full rescan inside the async endpoint
- tests: rewrite comfyui export-survives-edits to assert reconciliation,
  add link rewire, legacy per-node metadata, index_file, symlink and
  postMessage handshake/origin checks (57 passing); bump version to 1.2.2
